```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r}
con = DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "../data/midwest_airbnb_extended.db")
listings     = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "listings") |> tibble::as_tibble()
availability = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "availability_monthly") |> tibble::as_tibble()
reviews      = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "reviews_monthly") |> tibble::as_tibble()
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
```

## Task 1
```{r}
# Group listings by host and count how many listings each host owns
host_counts <- listings |>
  dplyr::group_by(host_id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(listing_count = dplyr::n())

# Join each host's listing count back onto every individual listing
listings_with_counts <- listings |>
  dplyr::left_join(host_counts, by = "host_id")

# Keep hosts with 10+ listings, then count how many of the hosts qualify
host_counts |>
  dplyr::filter(listing_count >= 10) |>
  dplyr::summarise(number_of_hosts = dplyr::n())

# Find the percent of Chicago listings who are owned by hosts with 10+ listings
listings_with_counts |>
  dplyr::filter(city == "Chicago") |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    percent = mean(listing_count >= 10) * 100
  )
```

## Task 2
```{r}
# Keep listings that meet the requirements for a family of 4
family_listings <- listings |>
  dplyr::filter(
    room_type == "Entire home/apt",
    accommodates >= 4,
    number_of_reviews >= 10,
    review_scores_rating >= 4.8
  )
# Create a price per person column by dividing price by number accommodated
family_listings <- family_listings |>
  dplyr::mutate(price_per_person = price / accommodates) # mutate() creates/changes columns
# Find the median price per person and number of listings for each city/neighborhood
neighbourhood_summary <- family_listings |>
  dplyr::group_by(city, neighbourhood) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median_price_per_person = median(price_per_person, na.rm = TRUE),
    number_of_listings = dplyr::n()
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(number_of_listings >= 20) # Keep only neighbourhoods with at least 20 qualifying listings
# Filter the table to Columbus only
neighbourhood_summary |>
  dplyr::filter(city == "Columbus") |>
# Arrange those neighborhoods from lowest median price per person to highest
  dplyr::arrange(median_price_per_person)
```

## Task 3
```{r}
# Group listings by city and room type
earnings_summary <- listings |>
  dplyr::group_by(city, room_type) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    dplyr::across(
      c(price, reviews_per_month, estimated_revenue_l365d), ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
      )
  )
earnings_summary |>
  dplyr::filter(
    city == "Twin Cities",
    room_type == "Entire home/apt"
  )
```

## Task 4
```{r}
# Group listings by city and sort estimated revenue from highest to lowest
revenue_ranked <- listings |>
  dplyr::group_by(city) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(estimated_revenue_l365d), .by_group = TRUE)
# Mark whether each listing falls within the top 10% of revenye earners in its city
revenue_ranked <- revenue_ranked |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    top_10 = dplyr::row_number() <= ceiling(0.10 * dplyr::n())
  )
# Find the percent of Columbus revenue earned by the top 10% of listings
revenue_ranked |>
  dplyr::filter(city == "Columbus") |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    percent_top_10 = 
      sum(estimated_revenue_l365d[top_10], na.rm = TRUE) /
      sum(estimated_revenue_l365d, na.rm = TRUE) * 100
  )
```

## Task 5
```{r}
# Keep only October 2026 availability data
october_availability <- availability |>
  dplyr::filter(month == "2026-10")
# Keep only entire home listings
entire_homes <- listings |>
  dplyr::filter(room_type == "Entire home/apt")
# Join October availability data to the entire home listings
october_homes <- entire_homes |>
  dplyr::left_join(october_availability, by = "id")
# Mark whether each entire home listing is mostly taken
october_homes <- october_homes |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    mostly_taken = nights_available < 0.5 * nights_in_month
  )
# Find the percent of entire homes that are mostly taken in each city
mostly_taken_summary <- october_homes |>
  dplyr::group_by(city) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    share_mostly_taken = mean(mostly_taken, na.rm = TRUE) * 100
  )

mostly_taken_summary
```

## Task 6
```{r}
# Join monthly reviews to the listing information 
reviews_with_city <- reviews |>
  dplyr::left_join(listings, by = "id")
# Keep only July 2025 through June 2026
reviews_year <- reviews_with_city |>
  dplyr::filter(
    month >= "2025-07",
    month <= "2026-06"
  )
# Find the total number of reviews for each city in each month
monthly_reviews <- reviews_year |>
  dplyr::group_by(city, month) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    total_reviews = sum(reviews, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
# Keep only Twin Cities and sort from most reviews to fewest
twin_cities_reviews <- monthly_reviews |>
  dplyr::filter(city == "Twin Cities") |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(total_reviews))
twin_cities_reviews |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    busiest_to_quietest = max(total_reviews) / min(total_reviews)
  )
```

## Task 7
```{r}
# Keep entire homes with a known Superhost status
# %in% keeps host marked "t" (Superhost) or "f" (not Superhost) and excludes NA
superhost_homes <- listings |>
  dplyr::filter(
    room_type == "Entire home/apt",
    host_is_superhost %in% c("t", "f")
  )
# Find the median price and rating for Superhosts and non-Superhosts in each city
superhost_summary <- superhost_homes |>
  dplyr::group_by(city, host_is_superhost) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median_price = median(price, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_rating = median(review_scores_rating, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
# Calculate the Superhost price premium in each city
superhost_premiums <- superhost_homes |>
  dplyr::group_by(city) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    premium = median(price[host_is_superhost == "t"], na.rm = TRUE) -
              median(price[host_is_superhost == "f"], na.rm = TRUE)
  )
# Square brackets tell R to only use the values that meet the specified condition
superhost_premiums
```

## Task 8
```{r}
# Find listings that do not have any matching rows in the availability data
missing_availability <- listings |>
  dplyr::anti_join(availability, by = "id") # anti_join shows me what doesn't match
# Count the total number of listings with no availability data
missing_availability |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    number_missing = dplyr::n()
  )
# Count the total number of listings with no availability data
missing_availability |>
  dplyr::group_by(city) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    number_missing = dplyr::n()
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(number_missing))
```
